title: CATL, Innolight Join Hong Kong Tech Index in AI Revamp
summary: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Tech Index expands to 50 stocks, adding CATL and Innolight to better capture AI hardware boom. Changes take effect December 7, 2026.
body_markdown:
**Officially launched on December 7, 2026.**


#### 💡 TL;DR


- Hong Kong's Hang Seng Tech Index will expand from 30 to 50 stocks on December 7, 2026, adding AI hardware leaders CATL and Innolight.
- The overhaul aims to better represent China's technology landscape after the index lagged regional peers by over 30% this year.
- New entrants will trigger $33.5 billion in passive fund inflows as 70% of additions focus on advanced hardware and AI automation.


Hong Kong's benchmark technology stock gauge is undergoing its most significant restructuring in years, expanding from 30 to 50 constituents to better capture the artificial intelligence hardware boom. Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. and Zhongji Innolight Co. are among the expected additions when Hang Seng Indexes Co. announces its quarterly review results after market close on November 19, 2026, with changes taking effect December 7, 2026.


The overhaul addresses years of investor criticism that the index failed to represent China's evolving technology landscape. The gauge has tumbled more than 30% this year as heavily weighted Chinese internet giants and automakers dragged on returns, while regional competitors surged on AI-driven rallies.


## Advanced Hardware Takes Center Stage


Approximately 70% of the new additions will be advanced hardware companies, according to Mizuho analyst Willer Chen. The expansion follows a wave of high-tech manufacturing IPOs in Hong Kong over the past two years. Beyond CATL and Innolight, potential joiners include chip designer Shanghai Biren Technology Co., printed circuit board maker Victory Giant Technology Huizhou Co., humanoid robot producer UBTech Robotics Corp., and e-commerce operator Shein Global Holdings Ltd.


Jason Lui, head of APAC equity derivatives strategy at BNP Paribas, notes the changes "enable the index provider to incorporate more technology hardware and high-tech manufacturing companies, reflecting significant shifts in the Hong Kong equity market structure in recent years." The move positions the index to compete with Asian rivals that have capitalized on AI infrastructure demand.


## Release Date and Market Impact


Officially announced on November 19, 2026, with implementation set for December 7, 2026, the expansion will trigger substantial capital flows. Stocks entering the Hang Seng Tech Index will see meaningful inflows from $33.5 billion worth of passive funds tracking the gauge, according to Bloomberg Intelligence. Special situations investors are already positioning on likely inclusion candidates while betting against probable deletions.


The 50-member Hang Seng China Enterprises Index may simultaneously add Hua Hong Grace Semiconductor Ltd. and Z.AI Co., while removing Shenzhou International Group Holdings Ltd. and Postal Savings Bank of China Co. The flagship Hang Seng Index could gain five constituents, including Zijin Gold International Co. and Yum China Holdings Inc., reaching its target member count of 100.


## AI and Robotics Focus


The rebalancing reflects Hong Kong's strategic pivot toward artificial intelligence, robotics, and cloud computing sectors. CATL, the world's largest electric vehicle battery manufacturer, brings exposure to energy storage critical for AI data centers. Innolight specializes in optical interconnect solutions essential for high-speed data transmission in AI training clusters.


Other sectors represented in potential additions include automation technologies and cloud infrastructure providers. Chen's analysis suggests China International Capital Corp. shares this view, with both firms projecting AI-related companies will dominate the expansion slate. The index now better mirrors the hardware-intensive reality of modern AI deployment, moving beyond its previous concentration in consumer internet platforms.


## What This Means


The Hang Seng Tech Index expansion marks Hong Kong's effort to reclaim relevance in Asian technology benchmarking after a year of underperformance. By prioritizing AI hardware and manufacturing over legacy internet stocks, the index acknowledges the infrastructure-driven nature of the current technology cycle. For investors, the December 7 effective date creates a clear timeline for portfolio adjustments, while passive fund managers face a substantial rebalancing obligation. The move may catalyze similar index reforms across Asian markets seeking to capture artificial intelligence value chains beyond software.
